lines: - **Opening and closing a quest is smooth,** as on the desktop. Tap the caret and the quests below glide down, uncovering its subtasks as they fade in. Close it and the subtasks fade where they are while the quests below glide up over them, like a curtain. Nothing jumps at the start or the end, and if you tap again halfway, it turns around. The same on COMPLETED, and with a long-press (all quests at once).
- **The caret turns a little slower,** in step with the motion below it.
A visual pass: quest_log now looks like a lit terminal screen.

- **The XP bar is a terminal gauge,** as on the desktop: 20 blocks between brackets, each lighting up as you earn it, brightest at the leading edge. The XP you've earned in this level reads first, in bright.

- **A lit screen behind the title.** A faint green phosphor glow and fine scanlines sit behind the top panel and every page's header (Settings, Help, What's new, Trash), and the dividers under them are lit in the middle.
- **The boot screen warms up like an old monitor:** the text glows, and a soft band passes down the screen once.

- **Lit feedback when you press.** The header and close buttons light their frames, and rows in menus, Settings and Move to… light up from the left edge. A selected option (priority, repeat, search filter) glows like the selected tab.
- **Menus and sheets** have a lit top edge, and their `>` prompt glows.
- **Messages** (the UNDO toast and tips) have a lit left edge.
- **Settings and What's new read more clearly:** each section title is followed by a rule that fades out, and settings that are ON glow.
- **The list fades out** just above the `> new quest` bar, instead of being cut off.
- **On an empty list,** the prompt glows and LOAD EXAMPLE TASKS stands out as the thing to do.

- **Fixed: a long quest title no longer flickers while you type.** From about three lines on, the whole title flashed with every letter. The cause was the quest title's capitals: on Android, drawing typed text in capitals rewrites the field with each keystroke. While you edit a quest, its title now shows exactly as you type it, and it's back in capitals as soon as you're done (it was always saved as typed).

- **Steadier typing near the keyboard.** The list only scrolls to keep your text in view when a line is really hidden, and only checks when the text box actually changes height, not on every keystroke.

- **Fixed: completing a quest ends smoothly.** After the burst, the quest slides away and fades, then the quests below glide up into its place in one smooth motion. Before, the space closed in uneven steps, because the list had to redo its layout for every frame, a little late each time. Now the glide runs entirely on the phone's display thread, with nothing for the app to catch up on, the same as the desktop version.
- **No more little jump at the end,** including when the quest at the top of the list leaves: the next quest's divider is already where it belongs.
Your quests in Obsidian (or any Markdown app).

- **New: Markdown sync, in Settings → Data.** The first time, tap **Set up Markdown sync…** and choose a folder, such as your Obsidian vault. quest_log writes **quest_log.md** there with all your quests and objectives. After that the button reads **SYNC**: tap it to update that same file, which is overwritten rather than duplicated. **Change folder…** moves it somewhere else, and **Stop Markdown sync** forgets the folder (the file stays).
- **Made to make sense in Obsidian:**
- one heading per tab (DAILY, MAIN, MISC), then COMPLETED;
- each quest is a checkbox, with its objectives nested under it;
- notes appear as a quote under their task;
- due dates, priorities, repeats and completion dates use the Obsidian Tasks plugin's format (📅 ⏫ 🔁 ✅), so that plugin can list what's due, sort and filter, and the due time is shown as 🕐;
- the note starts with properties (when it was synced, counts, level, XP) that Obsidian and Dataview can read.
- The note is a copy: change tasks in the app, and the next SYNC replaces the file. Trash isn't included. The JSON backup works exactly as before.
Polish: the keyboard, shorthand, a smoother finish, and a subtle glow.

- **Fixed: the keyboard opens when you add a subtask.** The same goes for every field that opens by itself: a new subtask (from `+`, `+ SUB` or the hold menu), notes, and the quick-add bar when it's asked to take focus. Before, the field could open without a keyboard until you tapped it.

- **Shorthand chips show just above the text you're typing,** small and quiet, in the same style when adding and when editing. Typing `@tomorrow 10am` shows `◔ TOMORROW 10:00` right over the line, not hidden under the keyboard.

- **Fixed: the `> new quest` bar hanging in the middle of the screen.** The bar now rides the keyboard only while you're typing in it. Both keyboard trackers can end typing, and the bar checks itself regularly while it's up. If it ever happens again, long-press the title for the developer screen, which has a KEYBOARD LOG to send me.

- **Completing a quest is smooth to the end.** It slides away, and then the list closes the gap: the quests below glide up instead of jumping. The same happens when you swipe a task away, or restore or delete one on COMPLETED.
- **Nothing jumps away while you work.** Ticking off an objective no longer sends its quest to the top mid-tap. The list sorts itself again when you switch tabs. New quests still appear at the top.
- **A subtle glow:** the title, the selected tab and the ACTIVE / COMPLETED bar, the quick-add field while you type, the toolbar and menu icons, and UNDO.
- **The ACTIVE · COMPLETED switch is 10% smaller.**
